source_scratch_dir: scratchpad/deep/maker/ (5 harvest chunks + aggregate.py/.md/.json; NOT committed, raw caches too large / superseded by this compact file)
fill_model_as_harvested: canonical scout sec.3: definite fill = trade print with taker_side=='no' and yes_price_c < P after hypothetical placement; ambiguous print at yes_price_c==P gets a 50% credit haircut. $0 maker fee on all KXHIGH*/KXLOWT* series (fee_type=quadratic, verified live). CRITICAL UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION in the harvest: every simulated bid is treated as a genuinely RESTING order regardless of the best ask at placement time -- i.e. it never checks whether the hypothetical bid price >= the prevailing ask, which is the condition under which a real limit order would cross the spread and execute immediately as a TAKER fill instead of resting. This assumption is what the verifier panel falsified (see verified_strict below).

naive_headline_grand_table.note: AS-HARVESTED table, reproduced verbatim from aggregate.json. REFUTED for the post-lock arm by the verifier panel's live candlestick/trade-tape audit -- kept here ONLY as the documented starting point the panel audited, not as a usable result. See verified_strict for the number that survives.

taker_baseline_comparison.units_note: As given by the orchestrator, units unresolved -- could be literal 0.15 cents/contract or a 15-cent (0.15 dollar) net edge. The whole-cents reading (~15c net) is more consistent with every other figure in this study and is treated as primary; either reading is moot now that the maker headline itself is refuted (see verdict).

panel_verdict_summary: REFUTED on the headline. Live 1-min candlestick audit of the post-lock P=93 cell found that for the large majority of simulated 'resting maker bids', the best ask at the simulated placement time was AT OR BELOW the bid price P=93c -- meaning a real limit order at that price would have crossed the spread and executed immediately as a TAKER fill, not rested as a maker order. These are the deployed taker bot's own trade opportunities relabeled at an artificial maker price, not a distinct maker edge.

panel_findings.summary: Post-lock 'resting maker bid' premise false for ~80% of the flagship P=93 cell: live 1-min candlestick audit of all 32 chunk_4 post-lock P=93 bids found 26/32 had best ask <= 93c at placement (examples: KXHIGHDEN-26JUL08-T93 ask=47c, KXLOWTCHI-26JUL02-T73 ask=17c, KXHIGHNY-26JUL08-T83 ask=46c), plus KSFO 26JUN11 (ask 73c) and 26MAY24 (ask 89c) from chunk_3, plus KBOS's single fill printing 34s post-lock. A limit YES buy at 93c against an ask of 5-89c executes immediately as a taker order and can never rest. ~19-20 of the naive 22.5 'maker fills' are mislabeled taker trades of the already-deployed lock strategy; Section 6 of the naive aggregate compared those trades to themselves.

Strict recompute (post-only, i.e. ask > P at lock, verified via live candlesticks + trade tape) on the flagship post-lock P=93 cell: restable bids ~5-8 of 58; verified genuine maker fills = 2 confirmed (KPHL KXHIGHPHIL-26JUN22-T87, ask 95c at lock, fill print 91c at +50s; KHOU KXLOWTHOU-26MAY19-T73, ask 96c at placement, fill at +199s), possibly 3 (KSFO KXHIGHTSFO-26JUL14-T81, ask 100c at lock, fill status unrecoverable from chunk_3 aggregates). Strict cell: n=2-3 fills, all wins, total gross +14 to +21 cents over the entire 65-day x 20-station frame (~$0.002/day at 1 contract). The naive 'n=22.5 fills, CI [0,15%] adverse selection, +7.00c/contract replicated at p<0.0001' does not survive.

0% adverse selection in the naive post-lock cell is near-tautological, not a market finding: every post-lock bid row has result='yes' because lock is defined by the same obs stream that determines the (monotone) daily extreme -- the outcome is already decided at placement. The day-clustered t-test (t=6.22, n=32) runs on a payout variable that cannot be negative by construction (0 or +7), so it only proves 'some fills occurred', not edge. The one real loss channel (Kalshi settlement/CLI vs ASOS-1min mismatch, breakeven failure rate ~7% at P=93) is unsampled at ~23 independent events.

'0/69 post-lock fills' triple-counts the same underlying events: one definite print below 93c fills the P=93, 95, and 97 cells simultaneously (chunk_4: 17/18/18 definite fills from ~18 underlying prints). Independent fill events are ~23-24, not 69; any pooled-CI reading of 69 is invalid. Per-P CIs in the naive table are the honest ones for THAT (flawed) fill model, but even those don't survive F1/F2.

Fill size / book capacity ignored: the harvest credits a full 1-contract fill on any qualifying print regardless of count_fp. Two of the 18 audited chunk_4 P=93 'fills' come from dust prints of 0.01 contracts (KXLOWTCHI-26JUL02-T73) and 0.10 contracts (KXLOWTDEN-26JUN04-T51). Total post-lock taker_side='no' volume at <=93c was only 1-13 contracts on 7/18 filled events. Bankroll extrapolations in the naive report (53 contracts/bid at $50 bankroll, +$1.28/day) exceed realized market capacity on multiple contributing events.

Zero-latency look-ahead: bids are 'placed' at the IEM asos1min observation valid-timestamp with 0s latency; 10/18 chunk_4 P=93 fills occur <2 minutes after lock (minimum 4.4s, KXHIGHNY-26JUL08-T83). asos1min data is not available at its valid time in real time, so these fills are uncapturable even before the marketability flaw (F1) is considered.

The same marketability flaw contaminates the pre-lock grid: a 93-97c bid placed while the rung is still 1-2F from its strike would typically cross a much lower ask, so the reported -55 to -69c/contract losses, 40-91% fill rates, and 66-72% adverse-selection rates in the naive pre-lock rows are not execution-realistic magnitudes (a crossing order fills ~100% instantly at ask, and losses are bounded by ask, not by P). The SIGN of the pre-lock result (negative EV) plausibly survives; no magnitude in that grid should be trusted or reused.

No harvest script filters is_block_trade (block prints do not sweep the book and cannot fill a resting bid); live audit shows all 18 chunk_4 P=93 fill prints were non-block, so no realized impact in the headline cell -- but the classifier is wrong in principle and should filter is_block_trade before any reuse.

Two scout choices hold up under live re-verification: taker_side semantics (no_price_dollars = 100 - yes_price on every audited print; taker_side='no' prints are genuinely bid-side executions), and the ==P 50% ambiguous-fill haircut is barely load-bearing (1 of 17.5 chunk_4 P=93 fills was ambiguous).

Aggregation arithmetic itself is clean: independent re-merge of all 5 chunk JSONs reproduces every naive grand-table row exactly (2,022 bids, 1,178 fills, 168 station-cells). The defect is entirely in the fill/marketability MODEL, not the summation.

verified_strict.scope: Flagship cell only: post-lock resting YES bid, P=93c (the naive headline's single best cell). Pre-lock cells and P=95/97 post-lock cells were NOT independently re-audited live by the panel at event level (F5 says pre-lock's sign plausibly survives but no magnitude does; no strict P=95/97 post-lock recount was reported) -- do not extrapolate this section's numbers to those cells.
verified_strict.method: Live 1-min candlestick check (yes_ask.low_dollars / yes_ask.close_dollars at the placement minute) applied to every naive post-lock P=93 bid; a bid only counts as genuinely 'restable' if the best ask at placement was strictly greater than 93c (post-only condition). Restable bids were then checked against the trade tape for an actual fill print, same definite/ambiguous rule as the naive model.
verified_strict.restable_bids_denominator_note: out of the naive model's 58 total post-lock P=93 bids across 16 stations

fills.status: possible_not_confirmed -- fill status not recoverable from chunk_3 aggregates

verified_strict.gross_total_c_confirmed_range_note: 2 confirmed wins at P=93 payout (100-93=7c) = 14c; if the 3rd (KSFO) also confirms as a win, 21c. Over 65 days x 20 stations.
verified_strict.net_ev_c_per_contract_note: identical +7.00c/contract payout math to the naive model when a fill IS genuine (100-P for a win, $0 maker fee) -- the panel's correction is entirely to n (how often a genuine, executable maker fill actually happens), not to the per-fill payout.
verified_strict.panel_reported_ci_range_note: panel's own prose cites an approximate '[0%, 66-80%]' band for this n=2-3 regime; this file's wilson95_ci fields are this synthesis's own Wilson-score recomputation (same method used throughout the naive aggregate for consistency) and may differ slightly in the upper bound depending on exact CI method (Wilson vs Clopper-Pearson) -- both agree the true rate could plausibly be well above 0% at this sample size.

capacity_and_execution_caveats: M3: at least 2 of the underlying post-lock print events across the wider (unaudited) chunk_4 P=93 set were dust-sized (0.01 and 0.10 contracts) -- even a genuine resting maker bid could not have been sized to the bankroll extrapolations in the naive report on those specific events; this caveat applies to the wider naive set, not necessarily to the 2-3 confirmed genuine fills above (their contract sizes were not in the panel's summary text).
M4: real-time capture requires beating asos1min's publication latency; a 0-latency backtest is not achievable live even for genuinely restable orders.
m1: is_block_trade must be filtered in any future harvest -- confirmed not to have contaminated the 18 audited chunk_4 P=93 prints, but the classifier logic that ignores it is wrong in principle.

recommendation.verdict: DO NOT DEPLOY the post-lock resting-maker-bid strategy as studied. The naive +7.00c/contract, n=22.5-fill headline is an artifact of simulating limit orders without checking whether they would cross the spread at placement; ~80-90% of its 'maker fills' are relabeled taker fills of the strategy already live in kwx_runner.py. The strict, execution-realistic version of the same idea (genuinely resting bids that never cross) has the same per-fill payout (+7.00c/contract when it does fill, $0 maker fee) but converts so rarely (2-3 confirmed genuine fills in 65 days x 20 stations) that it cannot be distinguished from noise (adverse-selection Wilson 95% CI upper bound 56-66% at this n) and contributes an economically negligible ~$0.002-0.003/day at 1 contract size.
recommendation.pre_lock_arm: Do not deploy in any form. Naive EV is deeply negative (-55c to -69c/contract) and the panel found even those magnitudes are inflated by the same marketability flaw (a bid that would actually cross fills near-instantly at the ask, not at P) -- but the SIGN (net-negative) is judged plausible to survive, so this arm should be treated as confirmed-bad, not merely unproven.
conditions_to_reopen_this_study: 1. Fix the fill simulator to enforce ask_c_at_placement > P (post-only / marketable-order check) before crediting any hypothetical fill as a maker fill, using the same live-candlestick method the panel used, applied to the FULL 58-bid post-lock set (all 16 stations) and to the pre-lock grid, not just the 32-bid chunk_4 slice.
2. Re-run with realistic latency (>=60-90s after an asos1min observation's valid time, matching the fastest realistic real-time feed available to kwx_runner.py) rather than 0s look-ahead.
3. Cap simulated fill size at the print's actual count_fp per event (no full-contract credit on dust prints), and filter is_block_trade=true prints out of the eligible-print set entirely.

4. Only re-open a go/no-go decision once the corrected post-lock P=93 cell reaches n>=30 independently-verified genuine maker fills (current: 2-3) -- below that, any CI is too wide to act on (see kwx_runner's own paper-gate bar: 'live == tested' at n>=~30 clustered, mirrored here).
staged_gate_if_reopened: Stage 0 -- Simulation fix: re-harvest with items 1-3 above; report strict-only numbers, no naive table reused for sizing.

Stage 1 -- Paper: run the corrected post-only maker logic as a passive add-on inside the existing paper harness (kwx_paper_gate.py-style, NOT a code change to it in this PR) for >=4-6 weeks to accumulate the n>=30 genuine-fill bar.
Stage 2 -- Paper gate: proceed only once corrected live-paper fills replicate a positive net EV with a Wilson 95% CI on adverse-selection that excludes >30%, at n>=30 clustered by station-day.

Stage 3 -- $10 canary: identical framework to KWX_DEPLOY.md's canary stage (1 contract/fire floor), run only as a supplement layered on top of the existing deployed taker strategy, sized so its rare fills cannot materially affect daily risk budget.
No stage in this list authorizes any code change in this PR -- this PR is documentation + a read-only reproduction harness only.
